text:
In Ottawa's first season since trading Brady Tkachuk to Florida, Tim Stützle has been the forward the Senators run through. He plays nearly 22 minutes a night, has 31 points in 25 games (13 goals), and Ottawa owns 59.7% of 5v5 expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice. He also has 51 hits, a lot for a playmaker.

Part of the scoring is hot finishing. He has 13 goals on 7.6 expected, shooting 22% against 18% last season, and that gap rarely holds. His last ten games are a better guide: 10 points, a little under what our numbers expect at his ice time, with his own shot quality down. The engine is passing and speed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards, and NHL Edge puts him in the 98th percentile for bursts over 20 mph. Evolving-Hockey noted the price last season: opponents got more chances with him on the ice than with all but 4% of forwards. Our numbers project about 96 points.
headline: Tim Stützle is the forward Ottawa runs through
